generationPrompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: original pixel-art character model sheet for a Final Fantasy Tactics Advance (2003 GBA) expansion. Create an entirely new HUMAN SAMURAI character design, faithfully matching original FFTA sprite proportions, pixel density, compact silhouettes, delicate clustered shading and three-quarter isometric camera. This is new artwork, NOT a Ninja reskin and NOT an illustration painted over an existing character. Human adult face visibly exposed, small native FFTA chibi proportions, flared red lacquer kabuto with restrained gold crescent crest, red lamellar shoulder plates and segmented skirt armor, dark indigo underclothes, simple boots, correctly sheathed katana at the hip. Clear samurai silhouette, coherent armor construction. Avoid mask, ninja hood, headband, oversized fantasy spikes, square robotic face and stiff symmetric block shapes. Produce ONE coherent model sheet with eight equally sized cells arranged four columns by two rows. Top row: relaxed battle-ready idle viewed southeast/front-right, southwest/front-left, northeast/back-right, northwest/back-left. Bottom row: corresponding same four directions with katana drawn in a plausible two-handed ready stance; preserve correct hand contact and blade direction. Same individual, costume, palette and scale in all eight cells. Each full body must fit a notional native 32x40 pixel canvas with roughly 18-24 pixel body width and 28-34 pixel height. Display the pixel art at a clean large integer nearest-neighbor enlargement so individual square pixels are visible, with no subpixel detail, blur, smoothing, gradients or painterly texture. Restrained GBA palette, around fifteen visible colors, dark colored outlines rather than thick pure-black comic outlines, light from upper left. Keep real transparent background, generous equal cell spacing, all bodies and weapons completely visible, no scenery, no floor shadows, no grid lines, no labels, no letters, no UI, no watermark. This is a design/import draft, not a claim that the image is already ROM-ready.
